title: Merge two sorted lists into a single sorted list using `Stream.concat(...).sorted()`.
shortTitle: Merge two sorted lists into a single sorted list using Stream.concat(...).sorted()
keyPoints: Stream.concat(a.stream(), b.stream()).sorted().toList() merges and sorts two lists
concat creates a lazily concatenated stream of all elements from both lists
sorted() re-sorts everything in O((m+n) log(m+n)), not exploiting pre-sortedness
For optimal O(m+n) merge, use a classic two-pointer algorithm instead
concat preserves duplicates; add distinct() for a merged unique set
Use the stream form for readability on moderate data; reserve two-pointer for large lists

s1_definition.oneliner: Stream.concat(a.stream(), b.stream()).sorted().toList() appends both streams and sorts the combined result into a single ordered list.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Stream.concat** creates a lazily concatenated stream of elements from a followed by b.
- **sorted()** orders the combined stream by natural order or a supplied comparator.
- **Does not exploit** pre-sortedness; re-sorts in O((m+n) log(m+n)).
- **Two-pointer merge** is the optimal O(m+n) alternative for already-sorted inputs.
- **distinct()** can be added to remove duplicates from the merged result.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya at the National Bank of India has two sorted transaction lists from two branches. She drops one list on top of the other and sorts the combined pile. It works, but a merge that walks both lists in order would be faster.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Merging two sorted lists uses Stream.concat to append one stream after the other and sorted to order the combined result. This is the simplest correct merge, though it re-sorts everything in O((m+n) log(m+n)) without exploiting the pre-sorted order.

For optimal O(m+n) performance, use a classic two-pointer merge that walks both lists in order. Add distinct() if the business wants a merged unique set. At the National Bank of India, Priya used this to combine sorted transaction lists from two branches into one unified report.

The concat approach is readable and correct for moderate data. Reserve the two-pointer merge for performance-critical paths or very large lists.

Remember one sentence: Stream.concat appends two streams and sorted re-orders the result, but it does not exploit pre-sortedness; for that, use a two-pointer merge.
